Subject: Weekly capacity thermostat: deal commit guardrails & shortfall plan

Team — kicking off this week's capacity thermostat thread. High-level goal: convert the pipeline snapshot into guardrails (min/target/max commit) for D-4829 and two smaller pilots so infra can reserve A100/H100 capacity without overcommitting our Q1 pool.

Attached: commitment_matrix_v2.xlsx (spread of asks by quarter), pipeline_snapshot_20261121.pdf, redwood-pricing-term-sheet.pdf.

Quick summary of asks:
- Sales (Laura/Ben): confirm the realistic committed range for Acme AI by Friday EOD (min = what they will definitely use; target = expected; max = aspirational).
- Finance (Karthik): confirm breakpoints for billing/commit thresholds and whether we can accept a 10% overprovision buffer in Q1 without additional CAPEX signoff.
- Infra (Grace): confirm how many reserved slices we can lock for Q1 given current commitments and the burst pool delta. If we need to reorder hardware types (A100 -> H100) call it out.

Proposed thermostat approach (for discussion):
1) Set a min/target/max commit per deal. Reserve the target. Keep a soft buffer equal to max(target * 0.10, 4 GPUs) inside burstable pool.
2) If weekly pipeline moves push projected utilization above 85% of targeted reserve, trigger canary buys and sales approvals.
3) Maintain a shortfall runbook: convert non-critical reserved slots to preemptible, fast-failover to hosted, and engage finance for reallocation.

Action: I put initial numbers in the matrix (column: min/target/max). Laura/Ben please update with customer-validated numbers; Sarah — if Acme has an updated forecast, please attach it.

Marcus
Marcus Lin

Adding infra numbers and a shortfall plan. Summary:
- Current Q1 reserved pool: 180 H100-equivalent slots (after existing contracts).
- Active target reservations proposed this week (across new deals): 42 slots. That pushes expected committed utilization to ~68%.
- If Acme hits max=12 and two other prospects convert, utilization moves to ~82% — still under our 85% soft threshold but removes runway for unexpected ramps.

Suggested guardrails:
1) Approve target-based reservation for Acme at 9 slots; hold additional 3 in a 2-week canary state (tagged 'pre-reserve') until contracts signed.
2) Finance okay with 10% soft buffer but wants explicit billing triggers at commit thresholds (6, 9, 12) so we can invoice early if customer moves from min->target.
3) Shortfall play: convert the oldest non-critical reserved slices to preemptible (60% cost savings) and notify customer 7 days ahead.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/D-4829 (tracking). See drive folder for the staging runbook.

Ben Carter

Appreciate the fast turn. Final decisions here to lock into this week's reserve cycle:
- Acme: min=6 / target=9 (reserve 9 for Q1); mark extra 3 as pre-reserve tagged in infra for 14 days pending contract sign.
- Contract clause: allow conversion of up to 2 reserved slots to burst in month 1 without penalty; finance to capture billing trigger language at 6->9 and 9->12.
- Infra: Ben, mark 9 slots as reserved (H100-preferred) and flag the 3 pre-reserve slots. If H100 supply arrives earlier than expected, we will migrate the pre-reserve to H100; otherwise they'll be A100-equivalent.

Open items (owners):
- Finance (Karthik): provide exact billing clause language by EOD Monday.
- Legal/Sales (Laura): finalize the SLA addendum and the month-1 conversion clause with Acme.
- Infra (Grace/Ben): confirm reservation ticket and tagging; ensure runbook has the 7-day customer notice for preemptible conversion.

I'll close this thread once we have the legal text and Karthik's billing triggers. Thanks everyone — nice example of thermostat approach working.
